summary: Identity attribute namespace collision prevents bastion SSO login for users with long service prefixes
summary_detail: Multiple engineers reported users unable to complete SSO login to the internal bastion host. Failures correlated to accounts with long service/team prefixes (e.g., svc-payroll-analytics-... ) or duplicated short names shared between service accounts and user accounts. The bastion session parser was truncating or overwriting the identity attribute namespace, causing authz checks to fail.
description:
Issue summary:
- Users with long or colliding identity attribute namespaces (department/service prefix + username) received a 403 during SSO completion to the bastion host.
Impact:
- ~18 engineers and several CI service accounts could not start interactive bastion sessions for ~3 hours in us-west.
- Blocked access to internal-only diagnostics and runbook execution for oncall.
Environment:
- prod, us-west; identity-proxy v2.13.1; bastion session parser 1.7.0.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Ensure user identity has a long attribute in Okta: departmentPrefix-userName (e.g., svc-data-analytics-longprefix-jdoe)
2) Initiate SSO login to bastion via console (electron app) or CLI plug-in
3) Observe that callback from identity-proxy returns 200 but the bastion session initialization returns 403 with 'principal namespace mismatch'
observed_behavior: SSO flow completes at identity-proxy; callback shows user identity attributes present. Bastion rejects the session with 403 'namespace collision' logged by session-parser. The session object shows truncated 'identity_namespace' or a replaced value (e.g., 'svc-data-analytic' instead of full 'svc-data-analytics-longprefix-jdoe').
expected_behavior: Identity attributes should be forwarded intact from identity-proxy to bastion session-parser and used for RBAC lookups. No truncation or overwriting should occur for identity namespace fields.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Okta SCIM or attribute mapping truncated value during SCIM sync. Verified by pulling raw callback payloads from identity-proxy logs — full attribute present. Root cause reproduced in staging: session-parser module applies legacy normalization that strips trailing tokens after 20 chars to match old schema. This normalization predated the current naming convention which now frequently exceeds 20 chars.
- Confirmed no recent Okta mapping changes (checked audit logs).
- Triage with SRE and Identity team at 09:40; created hotfix branch on identity-proxy to bypass parser normalization where upstream attribute is already namespaced.
- Cross-checked GraphQL RBAC service: lookup succeeded when given the full namespace; failure happens only when session-parser produces truncated key.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Aisha Nair (Support): Reproduced in staging. Identity-proxy shows full attr. Suspect session-parser normalization.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Priya Shah (Identity): Confirmed legacy normalization rule in session-parser. Preparing PR to remove 20-char truncate where identity_namespace present.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Liam O'Hara (Eng, assignee): Deployed hotfix to canary hosts in us-west. Verified two affected users could login. Rolling to rest of production.
2026-03-11 08:03 - Oncall (SRE Rotation): Monitored; no new 403s related to namespace collisions observed after rollout.
root_cause_analysis: Legacy session-parser normalization truncates identity_namespace to 20 characters to accommodate an older downstream index. Naming conventions expanded over time (service prefixes + descriptive team names), causing frequent collisions and RBAC mismatches. The identity-proxy was forwarding attributes correctly; the truncation was introduced in session-parser for historical compatibility and not updated with schema changes.
resolution: Applied hotfix: removed hard 20-char truncation in session-parser and added explicit validation so long namespaces are passed through. Deployed patch to us-west canary at 2026-03-10T10:30, full rollout completed by 2026-03-10T11:50. Backfilled the session store for affected sessions (recreated 18 sessions after user re-auth) and cleared stale entries. Added feature flag to revert if unexpected downstream issues arise.
